title: Japan Liquidity Enhancement Auction, remaining maturities 5–11 years (¥650bn anticipated) — the print that tests whether the family's "coupon preference" is identified at all
source: EST: mof.go.jp English September 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2609e.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 25,795 bytes) for this initial research; its table row reads 'Sep. 25, 2026 | Liquidity Enhancement Auction (remaining maturities of 5-11 years)'. TERMS ARE NOT ANNOUNCED: the Sep. 25 row carries no announcement href on 2026-09-09, while every row through Sep. 10 does, which matches MOF's own note that each issue amount is announced about one week prior — terms due ~2026-09-18. The ¥650bn size is anticipated, not announced, and the prior is MOF's own: its announcement pages print 'Offering Amount | About 650 billion yen' for TWENTY-FIVE CONSECUTIVE mid-zone auctions, 2024-08-22 through 2026-08-26, re-verified page by page this session (32 announcement pages auct20240115e … auct20260819e, all HTTP 200). CADENCE RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: MOF's 35 consecutive monthly calendars 2401e → 2611e (all HTTP 200) carry a mid-zone Liquidity Enhancement Auction in 35 of 35 months, labelled '5-15.5 years' through 2026-03-09 and '5-11 years' from 2026-04-16; the 1-5y zone runs 18 of 35 (odd months) and the 11-39y zone 17 of 35 (even months, December 2026 unpublished). Filed `estimate` on the standing counts — size anticipated rather than announced, reopened-issue list unpublished until the day, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy and the terms, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Proposed 2026-09-09 by the jgb-liquidity-enhancement-5-11y-2026-10-22 initial-research adjacency sweep (proposals/jgb-liquidity-enhancement-5-11y-2026-09-25.from-jgb-liquidity-enhancement-5-11y-2026-10-22.json, read as input and now shadowed by this canonical file); researched 2026-09-09 (docs/research/events/jgb-liquidity-enhancement-5-11y-2026-09-25.md). IT WAS PROPOSED TO SCORE THE FAMILY'S COUPON READING AND IT ENDS UP CORRECTING IT. This research built the first ISSUE-LEVEL panel of the instrument — 4,703 issue-auction observations across 48 auctions, this zone's 32 prints plus the 16 prints of the 1-5y zone the family had never read — and regressed each issue's takeup-minus-eligible share on its coupon, remaining maturity and float, with the standard errors block-bootstrapped BY AUCTION. THE COUPON COEFFICIENT'S 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVAL CONTAINS ZERO IN EVERY SPECIFICATION IN THIS ZONE, including with no controls at all (+0.205, CI −0.112 to +0.585). The only coefficient whose interval excludes zero here is log float, and it is NEGATIVE (−0.687, CI −1.265 to −0.126): bidders overweight SCARCE issues, and coupon rides along because old small-float paper is also high-coupon. OUT OF SAMPLE THE MONOTONE ORDERING IS REFUTED OUTRIGHT: in the 1-5y zone the LOWEST-coupon security (10-year, 0.100% weighted-average) is overweight at 1.07x and the HIGHEST (30-year, 2.507%) is underweight at 0.61x, with 5-year (0.713%) the most underweight security in the zone at 0.49x. AND THE '2026-08-26 BROKE RANKS' PRINT DECOMPOSES CLEANLY: its ¥401.2bn of 20-year takeup went to No.155-161 at 9.32-10.82 YEARS REMAINING — the longest 20-year paper in the band, overweights 1.22x to 7.64x — against 0.01x-0.51x for everything at 6.5-8.8y. It was a remaining-maturity take, not a coupon reversal; the sibling flagged that coupon and remaining maturity are the same variable inside one sector and then read the print through the coupon lens anyway. Sector-level ordering survives only in part: with auction-clustered intervals 10Y 0.64x (0.43-0.86) is genuinely below 20Y 1.31x (1.11-1.51), but 20Y and 30Y 1.64x (1.10-2.23) are NOT distinguishable at n=32. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low`: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure and no house playbook is rates-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
